summary: Plains of Otosan Uchi (issue #554): full engine rules for the two-Dynasty-card province, built against PR #544's now-merged view contract -- ProvinceState.CardId2, reveal-order choice (Left/Right), refill, Purchase/RecruitReserve from either slot, DestroyProvince's 10-Honor loss, single battlefield/shared adjacency (unchanged by construction), province-card targeting disambiguation (Shosuro Toson wired as the worked example) and the MRP errata (Region destroyed alone keeps the second slot's card, stops future refills). ProvinceView.DynastySlots/MatchView.PendingProvinceOrder populated (shared engine+view contract touchpoint, plus test-suite guard-test updates, hence the shared lane).
validation: Full Core suite: 2143/2143 passed (0 failures), including six new otosan-uchi-plains tests. dotnet build: 0 warnings/errors. Three pre-existing pinned guard tests (action-lock/InnateActionInventory, seppuku-timing/EveryPendingFieldIsClassified, engine-hooks/LegacyResume) updated to classify the new command types/state field and to prune nested new fields (not just top-level) when comparing against the historical save-compatibility fixture.
remaining: Not yet published as a playable card: no region-wave JSON entry exists, and this environment lacks the cwebp CLI build_catalogue_art.py needs to refresh catalogue-art.json/catalogue-art-pack.json from the already-local reference scan, so publishing was deliberately left for a follow-up (the art-pack-release skill) rather than partially done. Exercised only via the training-otosan-uchi synthetic fixture. Three of DiscardCurrentProvinceCard's four callers (EffectChoice.cs's generic branch, EmperorP5.cs's Mistrust, SeedsOfDecayBatch5.cs's Scorpion Sword) still pick the first occupied slot unconditionally on a two-slot province rather than asking; Toson was the one Mendon named as the worked example. ~14 narrower per-card province lookups elsewhere are untouched (documented in the decision doc) -- they throw rather than silently misbehave if ever they hit the second slot.
